he-qubo-tsp-encoding: Section II.A, p.2: the paper defines its own binary variable x_{u,j} for city u at position j. Read in context.
he-qubo-tsp-uniqueness-constraints: Section II.A, p.2, Eqs. 3 and 4: the two uniqueness constraints (each city once, each position one city) are the paper's own.
he-qubo-tsp-nonadjacent-constraint: Section II.A, p.3, Eq. 5: the paper states the non-adjacent-cities constraint as part of its own QUBO.
he-qubo-hamiltonian-penalty: Section II.A, p.3, Eq. 8: H = A*F + C, with A described as the balance between the constraint penalty and the path cost. The paper's own objective.
he-qa-time-dependent-hamiltonian: Section II.B, pp.3-4, Eqs. 13 and 14: the paper writes its annealing Hamiltonian H(t) = A(t)Hkin + B(t)Hpot with the stated start and end conditions on A and B.
he-qgnn-loss-definition: Section II.C, pp.4-5, Eq. 15: the QUBO-based loss is the paper's own method definition. The passage says the learning objective becomes finding low-energy states that obey the TSP constraints.
he-qgnn-heatmap-local-search: Section II.C, p.5: the paper states that a guided local search on the heatmap gives the final solution. The method is described in the same section.
he-qgnn-sylvester-details-omitted: Section II.C, p.5: the authors state that specific details of the Sylvester transformation matrix technique are not provided. It is a stated gap in their own description.
he-experiment-scope-n100-only: Section III.A, p.5: the authors state the memory limit and that only n = 100 experiments are done for QQA. Caveat: Table I (p.8) also lists QQA rows for TSP20 and TSP50, so the sentence is loose. The value reports the authors' statement only, so it holds.
he-experiment-baselines-from-literature: Section III.A, pp.5-6: results of some traditional algorithms were taken from the literature and the test set is that of Fu et al. 2021. Stated setup.
he-qqa-memory-limit: Section IV, p.7: the authors state that the long-term applicability of QQA is hindered by the memory overhead of simulating qubits, which exceeds 16 gigabytes at the time of writing. Stored value matches the passage.
he-qqa-simulation-platform: Abstract, p.1 and Section III.A, p.6: the authors state that the QQA-TSP demonstration uses quantum simulation platforms and that they used MATLAB's quantum computing toolbox to emulate annealing. The added MATLAB clause is in the passage. Own setup.
qsvm-qubo-encoding: Section 3.1, p.6, Eq. 4: the paper defines alpha_n as a sum of K binary variables with base B, B typically 2 or 10.
qsvm-penalty-term: Section 3.1, p.7, Eq. 6: the penalty term with positive coefficient xi controlling the strictness of the constraint is the paper's own definition.
qsvm-boltzmann-weighting: Section 3.2, pp.7-8, Eqs. 7 to 9: Boltzmann probability per solution and the probability-weighted alpha_n are the paper's own method.
qsvm-batch-processing: Section 3.3, p.9, Eqs. 11 and 12: nb = ceil(N/B) batches of B samples, B at most the qubit limit, one batch at a time, alpha and b stored per batch.
qsvm-ensemble-averaging: Section 3.3, pp.9-10, Eqs. 13 and 14: average of the batch predictions, class i if y_bar > 0, otherwise class j.
qsvm-one-vs-one-voting: Section 3.4, p.10, Eqs. 15 to 17: one classifier per class pair, one vote each, most votes wins.
qsvm-setup-hardware: Section 4, p.12: simulated CIM plus a real CIM from Beijing Boson Quantum Technology, the Qboson CIM 550W with 550 qubits. Stated setup.
qsvm-setup-banknote: Section 4.1, p.12: two banknote datasets, 250 training and 100 validation points, C and gamma 3 and 16, B and K 2, penalty 0.001. Stated setup.
qsvm-setup-iris: Section 4.2, p.14 and the Table 3 note: data volume within about 100 qubits, 40% of the data as test set (the paper says 'training set'), parameters 1, random state 42, three trainings each one-vs-one. The value repeats the paper's wording. Stated setup.
qsvm-future-work-limit: Section 5, p.16: the sentence follows the authors' remark that current devices still face qubit-count and error-rate limits. It states what is not yet done: scaling to larger datasets and error mitigation. The value says only that.
qgan-sim-only: Section 4, p.11: the study conducts simulations on PyTorch and Qiskit using MNIST. Stated setup.
qgan-hqcnn-architecture: Section 3.1, p.8: CNN with 3x3 convolution, max-pooling, ReLU, angle encoding, then a VQC of Ry, Rz and CNOT gates. The paper's own model.
qgan-qgan-architecture: Section 3.2, p.9: generator is a VQC plus a classical network, discriminator a classical fully connected network. The paper's own model.
qgan-training-parameter-shift: Section 2.3, p.7 and Algorithm 1, p.8: discriminator trained by backpropagation, generator by the parameter shift rule, with the other side fixed. It sits in the Preliminary section but Algorithm 1 is the QGAN training the paper uses. Value matches.
qgan-general-strategy: Section 3.3, p.9 and Algorithm 2, p.10 (train QGAN to convergence, generate, merge, retrain) and Section 4.2, p.13 (300 samples, 100 per class). The paper's own strategy and setup.
qgan-customized-strategy-test-set: Section 3.4, p.11 and Algorithm 3, p.12 (checked on the rendered page): four components, and the loop over Dtest counts errors per class to set R[i] = E[i]/Etotal. The paper's own algorithm.
qgan-table1-parameters: Table 1, p.12, checked on the rendered page: parameters 1,510,212; 3,346,476; 1,510,425; 4,414,537. Epochs 200, 200 / 500, 200, 500 for QGAN, DCGAN, GAN-1 and GAN-2.
qgan-table3-sample-allocation: Table 3, p.15, checked on the rendered page: generated 45, 11, 244; augmented 145, 111, 344; confidence 0.50, 0.48, 0.45. The sums are consistent (100 plus generated).
qgan-general-baseline-control: Section 4.3.1, p.15: the control generates 300 samples, 100 per class, and includes all without screening. Stated setup.
qgan-training-testing-100-per-class: Section 4, p.11: 'only 100 samples per class are used for training and testing', for the stated reason 'To simulate real-world data scarcity'. The paper's own setup. Split from he-simulation-scope at the team lead, 2026-11-06, Sprint 16 Manual Validation Q1 = 3 (split).
he-simulation-scope: Section 4, p.11: the three-class reduction is the paper's own stated limit, 'Due to the high computational cost of simulating large-scale quantum systems'. Split at the team lead, 2026-11-06, Sprint 16 Manual Validation Q1 = 3 (split): the 100-sample choice, made 'To simulate real-world data scarcity', is now qgan-training-testing-100-per-class.
svqx-gates-as-players: Section 2.1, p.4 and Section 3, p.8: gates (or groups) are players and the value function comes from measurement results. The paper's own approach.
svqx-additive-noise-scope: Section 2.2, p.4: the authors limit themselves to additive noise and call other noise representations an open question. Stated scope.
svqx-coalition-circuit-definition: Section 3.1, p.9, Eqs. 23 to 26: a coalition is a circuit of the coalition's gates plus the passive gates in R.
svqx-removal-scope: Section 5, p.27: the authors say other operations on gates outside the coalition could replace removal. This states that their method removes them (Fig. 3, Eq. 25) and does not cover alternatives.
svqx-no-quantum-extension: Footnote 3, p.8: classical (uncertain) Shapley values are applied to quantum gates, with no quantum extension of the concept. Stated scope.
svqx-scope-architecture-only: Section 1, p.2: the authors limit themselves to the second question, the effect of model architecture, not the inputs. Stated scope.
svqx-value-expressibility: Section 3.2, p.11, Eq. 36 and App. A: expressibility (a distance to the uniform unitary distribution, after Sim et al.) with a negative sign as the value function. The paper gives the estimator itself.
svqx-value-entangling-capability: Section 3.2, p.11, Eq. 37 and App. B: mean Meyer-Wallach measure over random parameters, value in [0, 1].
svqx-value-hellinger-fidelity: Section 3.2, p.12, Eq. 38 and App. C: Hellinger fidelity between QPU and noise-free simulator results as the value function; smaller values mean larger deficiencies.
svqx-value-execution-efficiency: Section 3.2, p.12, Eq. 39 and App. D: negative penalty per gate on the best transpilation, s1 < 0 and s2 < s1, and no QPU is used.
svqx-simulation-infinite-shots: Section 3.1, pp.10-11: in the paper's formalism a simulation is the case s to infinity in Eq. 17, so the bit-string distribution is exact. The paper's own definition.
svqx-appendix-expressibility-def: Appendix A, p.35, Eqs. 47 to 54: the KL divergence between the estimated fidelity distribution and the Haar distribution, whose density depends only on q. High value means low expressibility.
svqx-appendix-expressibility-shots: Appendix A, p.35: a SWAP test with s shots for each of cp pairs gives s*cp shots in total. A direct count from the paper's own estimator.
svqx-appendix-entangling-def: Appendix B, p.36, Eqs. 55 to 61: mean Meyer-Wallach measure over cs tomography states, s*cs shots in total.
svqx-appendix-efficiency-def: Appendix D, p.38, Eqs. 67 to 69: the estimated execution efficiency is the largest transpilation efficiency over all transpilations, the largest sum of gate penalties.
svqx-setup-software-data: Section 4, p.13: Python with Qiskit and an SVQX toolbox; the data is stated to be publicly available. Stated setup.
svqx-setup-devices: Section 4, p.13: idealized statevector and shot simulators; ibmq_ehningen and ibm_oslo, superconducting, from IBM Quantum cloud.
svqx-table1-device-specs: Table 1, p.38, checked on the rendered page: ehningen 27 qubits, QV 64, CX error 7.218e-3, T1 127.09 us, T2 143.27 us; oslo 7 qubits, QV 32, 9.748e-3, 148.03 us, 41.79 us. Values as provided by IBM.
svqx-qsvm-setup-featuremap: Section 4.1, p.13: two-qubit second-order Pauli-Z evolution circuit with 7r gates, r in {1, 2, 3}.
svqx-qsvm-setup-data: Section 4.1, p.13: artificial data set of [84], gap 0.3, 40 training and 1000 test points drawn uniformly with balanced labels, separable by construction with r = 2.
svqx-qpu-noise-setup-qsvm: Section 4.1, p.16: r = 1, six evaluations on ibmq_ehningen, K = 1, alpha = 1, so the only randomness is QPU error. Stated setup.
svqx-qnn-value-function: Section 4.2, p.18 and the Figure 13 caption: v(S) is the one-shot test accuracy of the circuit with gates from S union R, trained parameters fixed, on the shot simulator.
svqx-qgan-setup: Section 4.3, p.19 and Fig. 15: three qubits, 2^3 = 8 amplitudes, a discretized log-normal target, nine trainable parameters (theta in R^9).
svqx-qgan-hellinger-setup: Section 4.3, pp.19-20: Hellinger fidelity of state-simulator output against ibm_oslo, qubits 0-1-2 and 3-5-4, with and without MEM, three runs, K = 3, alpha = 1.
svqx-qgan-run-duration: Table 2, p.41, checked on the rendered page: run 1 of 0-1-2 from 2022-12-10 16:01:01 to 2022-12-11 19:12:15, 28 samples. The caption says the intervals include waiting times and MEM.
svqx-transpilation-setup: Section 4.4, p.22: estimated execution efficiency with s1 = -1 and s2 = -10, classical host only, 50 transpilation repeats, best taken, no measurements.
svqx-qaoa-setup: Section 4.5, pp.23-24 and Fig. 21 caption: seven vertices, ten edges, unique optimal cut of nine edges; depth 1 to 7; COBYLA, three runs per depth; state simulator. Stated setup.
svqx-qaoa-energy-excluded-pruning: Section 4.5, p.26: the energy is excluded from the layer analysis because it depends on parameters fixed on the full circuit. The value repeats the paper's reason.
svqx-toolbox-data-public: Section 1, p.3: a toolbox and the experiment data are stated to be publicly available online.
svqx-subset-coalitions-limit: Section 5, p.27: the authors say further research might be required for a more general analysis, especially at large scale. The lead-in 'results suggest' is hedged and is not contradicted. The caveat is the point of the sentence.
svqx-complexity-limit: Section 5, p.27: 'The high complexity, inherited from the classical SVs, is arguably the major limitation of the proposed SVQX approach.' A limit the paper states about its own method.
svqx-experiments: Section 5, pp.26-27 and Sections 4.1, 4.3, 4.4: five use cases, simulators plus two superconducting QPUs. QPU runs are the six ibmq_ehningen QSVM runs and the ibm_oslo QGAN runs; the QNN, QAOA and transpilation evaluations run on simulators or a classical host, as each section says. The 'only these' reading comes from the sections together, and each section supports it.

theory_low.he-qubo-ising-mapping: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section II.B, p.3, Eq. 10: s_i = 2x_i - 1 is the standard QUBO to Ising change of variables. The paper states it and does not prove the equivalence.

requote.he-simulation-scope: split at the team lead, 2026-11-06, Sprint 16 Manual Validation Q1 = 3 (split): the value keeps only the three-class reduction and its stated reason

value_replace.he-simulation-scope: The authors state that, because of the high computational cost of simulating large-scale quantum systems, the MNIST task is simplified to a three-class problem.
